MIT

plugins.description: Short model-generated recap under every completed turn in the DeepSeek Harness Web UI, plus an on-demand /recap command.
plugins.readme_text: # Turn Recap for DSH A persistent [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that writes a short, model-generated recap under every completed turn in the Web UI — and regenerates one on demand with `/recap`. English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## What it does - **After a turn the session goes quiet** a card appears at the end of that turn: one to three sentences saying what the turn accomplished and, only when it matters, what is still unfinished. The card waits out a quiet window (two minutes by default) and never appears for a turn you kept working past — it is a "where did I leave off" card, not a second summary of a reply you are still reading. The text follows the conversation's language. - **`/recap`** produces the same card for the latest turn on demand, immediately — useful when a turn never got its quiet window, when you scrolled past it, or when you want a fresh read of where things stand. - Turns that carry nothing to summarize (interrupted or failed turns, empty turns) produce no card, and subagent sessions are skipped by default. The card uses the host's theme tokens, so it follows light/dark and the active locale (English and Simplified Chinese dictionaries ship with the bundle). ## Install This package is a DSH bundle: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and a `dsh.client` half, so it installs into a profile with the launcher's own plugin command. Nothing is published to npm. ```bash # newest commit on the default branch dsh plugin add github:littepointR/dsh-turn-recap # or pin the tagged release dsh plugin add github:littepointR/dsh-turn-recap#v1.0.0 ``` `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory and selects the bundle when the install finishes. With HMR enabled in the profile's YAML the composition reloads immediately; otherwise the profile picks it up on the next start. Install into a named profile by passing it through: ```bash dsh plugin --profile add github:littepointR/dsh-turn-recap ``` The bundle patch adds one Loader row: ```yaml - insert: - id: turn-recap name: '@local/dsh-turn-recap' ``` ### From a checkout ```bash git clone https://github.com/littepointR/dsh-turn-recap.git dsh plugin --profile add link:D:/path/to/dsh-turn-recap ``` Or ask a DSH session to install the bundle from that directory with the profile's plugin manager. Reinstalling or toggling the plugin needs no Harness restart: disable and re-enable the row and the Host module is imported again. ## Configuration Every key is optional. Add a `config` block to the Loader row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — that layer survives package upgrades. | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | `false` unregisters the projection, the turn listener, and `/recap` | | `maxTokens` | `200` | Output budget of the recap request | | `temperature` | `0.2` | Sampling temperature | | `timeoutMs` | `12000` | Hard bound on one recap request, in milliseconds | | `digestChars` | `6000` | Size bound of the turn digest sent to the model | | `idleMs` | `120000` | Quiet window a finished turn must hold before its card may appear; `0` shows it immediately | | `skipSubagents` | `true` | Subagent sessions get no automatic recap | | `provider`, `model` | unset | Explicit route; by default the turn's own request route is reused | ```yaml - insert: - id: turn-recap name: '@local/dsh-turn-recap' config: maxTokens: 300 skipSubagents: false ``` ## How it works ``` agent/turn-stopping ──▶ digest the turn ──▶ model call ──▶ pending map │ turn/end (committed) ──▶ projection apply ──▶ recap projection ──▶ useProjection("recap") │ conversation.chat.turnTail ``` 1. **`agent/turn-stopping`** is the serial event the agent loop dispatches just before it commits `turn/end`. The plugin digests the turn from the session log — the user request, the newest tool calls (with failures marked), and the turn's *final* assistant reply — and asks the model that served the turn for a short recap. 2. The following **`turn/end`** commit folds the text into the client-visible **`recap` session projection**, so the card and the finished turn arrive in the same frame. 3. The Client half registers into the **`conversation.chat.turnTail`** slot and reads the projection with `useProjection("recap")`. Each entry carries a `revealAt` deadline: the card is held back until that instant passes **and** no newer turn has started, so the quiet window costs nothing and the card never interrupts active work. **Why a projection instead of a session event?** A plugin may not append new event types: a log carrying a type the build does not know cannot be reopened, and `appendPluginRecord()` is reserved for first-party experimental packages. The session projection is the supported carrier for session-derived client state. **Why is the recap produced before `turn/end`?** Projection state is folded synchronously from committed events and its Value is only re-read when a committed event changes that state. Producing the text while the turn boundary is still open is what lets the commitment bake it into state — the delayed *appearance* is a client-side rule over the stored `revealAt`, not a delayed request. **`/recap`** is a plain DSH command: it runs outside any turn, and its result travels in `command/done`. The Client half claims the command row through the `conversation.chat.commandview` slot under the `recap` key and renders the running, success, and failure states itself. ## Trade-offs and limits - **One extra model request per turn.** It is short, but it is billed by your provider; it does not appear in the session's token statistics because no assistant message is appended for it. - **The turn closes after the recap is ready.** Generation happens before `turn/end`, so a slow provider delays the boundary by up to `timeoutMs`. Failures and timeouts degrade to "no card", never to a failed turn. The quiet window delays only what you see, not what you pay. - **A card you never earned stays hidden.** If you send the next prompt before `idleMs` elapses, that turn gets no card; `/recap` is the escape hatch when you want one anyway. - **Recap text cannot be re-derived from the log.** It lives in the projection checkpoint, so it survives a restart; a projection cell rebuilt from the log alone (for example after the plugin is re-registered) starts empty. - **`stateVersion` gates cached wording.** Bumping it discards recaps cached under the previous digest rules instead of serving stale text. ## Development Both halves are dependency-free JavaScript: the Host half is plain ESM, the Client half is a module-loader factory that only asks the page for `react`. ```bash npm test # Host half under a fake Cordis context — needs nothing but Node npm run check # syntax-check every JavaScript entry point ``` The Host tests cover the projection fold, the turn digest, the `/recap` handler, and the failure paths, so most changes can be verified without a running Harness. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: Curated durable memory for DeepSeek Harness: automatic capture, progressive-disclosure recall, duplicate folding and conflict resolution, plus a sidebar management panel.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-memory-curator

Curated durable memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh): automatic
capture of decisions, corrections, prohibitions and open work; progressive-disclosure recall;
duplicate consolidation; and old-vs-new conflict resolution. Everything is local — one JSON
store under `$DSH_HOME`, no network of its own, no account, no API key. Model calls reuse the
Harness `llm` service, so memory inherits the user's provider, credentials and retry policy.

[中文说明](#中文说明)

## Install

A plain Cordis bundle: no build step, no runtime dependencies.

```bash
# 1. install it into the profile that runs your DSH
cd "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/desktop"    # your own profile directory
pnpm add link:/path/to/dsh-memory-curator

# 2. list it as a bundle in that profile's package.json, e.g.
#    "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [
#      "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-memory-curator" ] } }
```

Restart DSH. The host half mounts capture, recall, curation and the six `memory_*`
tools; the browser half adds the **Memory** entry to the left sidebar. The package ships
`cordis.patch.yml` — the patch DSH applies while composing the tree — so the plugin row
and its default configuration come from the package itself.

DSH's plugin manager (Settings → Plugins) accepts the same `link:` spec and performs both
steps for you; a page refresh is enough after that, no rebuild.

## What it does

| | Behaviour | How |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Auto-capture** | When a turn ends, the conversation is distilled into durable entries worth keeping across sessions: designated technical references, architecture decisions, explicit corrections, prohibitions, and unfinished work. | A fire-and-forget listener on `session/event` (`turn/end`) sends the new messages to one bounded auxiliary LLM call; the validated candidates are persisted. Memory work can never delay or fail a turn. |
| **B. Progressive recall** | Each turn gets a bounded one-line-per-entry index: the entries that change behaviour (decisions, corrections, prohibitions, open work) come first, then the most recent facts. Full text is fetched only on demand. | A resident catalog is injected into the system prompt (tier 0). `memory_search` returns short digests with ids (tier 1). `memory_detail` returns the complete entry (tier 2) and records the read, which feeds the ordering and the decay pass. The standing prompt cost stays flat as the store grows. |
| **C. Curation** | Duplicate knowledge folds into one entry; a newer decision on the same subject retires the outdated one. | A deterministic pass runs on every insert and periodically: same-subject decisional entries conflict, the newer wins, the older is kept as history with a `supersededBy` pointer. A model-assisted pass adjudicates the similar-subject pairs the deterministic pass cannot settle, biased toward `coexist` so a true memory is never wrongly retired. |

## What memory does not record

The plugin deliberately does not overlap with the artifacts a project already keeps. Any one
of these tests means *record nothing*:

| Test | Where that information belongs instead |
|---|---|
| Would a future session get it from the repository? Architecture, file paths, build and test commands, dependency lists, directory layout, git history. | The code and git themselves. |
| Is it a project-level instruction — a convention, an "always/never" rule? | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, where every teammate and every tool sees it. Memory is machine-local and invisible to the rest of the team. |
| Is it task state — progress, next steps, a worked-off plan? | `STATE.md`, a todo list, or the issue tracker. |
| Is it a report that something was just done? "published the repository", "rewrote the history", "added a section". | The artifact is its own record. |

To make the first two decidable rather than a matter of taste, every distillation call carries
the repository context: the bounded text of `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` when they exist, plus the
names of `README.md`, `STATE.md`, `TODO.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/`. Reads are cached by mtime and size, so a quiet repository costs a
few `stat` calls per turn.

What is left is the part with no other home: environment and tooling traps, the user's own
preferences and corrections, and facts about this machine that the repository cannot know.

Credentials are the one case where a prompt is not enough. `lib/store.js` redacts
credential-shaped strings (`sk-…`, `ghp_…` / `github_pat_…`, `AKIA…`, `xox…`, JWTs, PEM private
keys) at the single write choke point every path goes through, so an auto-capture, a tool call
and a panel paste are all covered. Redaction beats rejection: the sentence around a leaked key
is usually the part worth keeping, so the entry survives with `[redacted]` where the secret was.
The patterns name credential shapes, not "anything that looks random" — a commit id or a sha256
digest is untouched.

Because memory is machine-local, the agent is also told — in the resident recall guidance — to
**promote** an entry that is really a project rule into `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` and then
`memory_forget` it, so the two cannot drift apart.

## Forgetting

Memory that is never read still costs prompt bytes in every injection, so the store does not
only grow. Three things retire an entry, and none of them deletes text — a retired entry keeps
its id, its text and its history, and simply stops being recalled:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `superseded` / `merged` | A newer statement on the same subject replaced it, or a duplicate folded into it. Carries a `supersededBy` pointer. |
| `forgotten` | Someone retired it on purpose (`memory_forget`, or the panel's Forget). |
| `decayed` | Nothing read it for `decayAfterDays` and it is past `decayGraceDays` of age. |

Decay refuses to touch the two kinds whose value is not a function of readership: decisional
entries (including `open`), because a prohibition nobody has tripped yet is still binding, and
`reference` entries, because they are consulted rarely by nature. "Read" means `lastRecalledAt`
when the entry has been read, else its own age. Set `decayAfterDays: 0` to turn decay off.

## Measuring recall

The plugin records what memory is *used*, not only what it stores: `memory_detail`
marks the entry it opened (`recallCount`, `lastRecalledAt`), the panel shows that
count per entry and the store-wide total in its header, and an entry that was
just read counts as fresh when the index is ordered — being used is not punished
by age.

`npm run audit:recall` reads DSH's own session logs (the plugin records no recall
events) and reports what actually happened: which memory tools the agent reached
for, how many entries it opened in full, how often the index had to hide entries,
and which entries are hidden right now. It is read-only, and it decodes a session
log frame by frame, because DSH writes one zstd frame per record.

A run over the first ~7 hours of real use:

```text
tool calls     memory_add=16  memory_detail=13  memory_forget=10  memory_stats=4
               memory_search=0  memory_curate=0
readership     9 of 55 active entries ever opened in full
index          166 injections, 26% of them had to hide entries
eviction       13 of 52 visible entries hidden — 5 decisional, 6 of them read
```

That measurement drove two decisions: the index is now layered (rules and
decisions first, then the most recent facts) because a purely newest-first index
let fresh task narration evict the platform knowledge that had actually been
read, including a live prohibition; and the footer now names `memory_search`
instead of only counting what was withheld.

**Subagents get the tools but not the resident index.** DSH marks a delegated
session in its header (`origin: 'subagent'`, `delegationDepth`), and over three
subagent sessions each one received a full catalog while the three together made
a single memory call. They can still search on demand.

### The first cleanup, as a worked example

After that measurement the store was pruned by hand against the admission tests above (a backup
is taken first, and the pru

plugins.description: Per-conversation timestamp toggle for the dsh Web composer: each submitted message is followed by a hidden context message carrying the current local time.
plugins.readme_text:
# @local/dsh-send-timestamp

在 dsh Web 客户端的聊天输入框工具栏右侧加一个「时间戳」开关。开启后，你提交的每条消息后面会跟一条**只带时间戳的隐藏消息**：对话界面里看不到它，但会话记录里存着、送交模型时也在。

```
对话界面：  你： 帮我看下这个报错

会话记录与模型收到：
  你： 帮我看下这个报错
  （隐藏）[10-16 10:23:45]
```

## 行为

| 规则 | 取值 |
|---|---|
| 默认格式 | `[MM-DD HH:mm:ss]`（月-日 + 时:分:秒，24 小时制，本地时间，各段补零） |
| 预设 `time` | `[HH:mm:ss]`（纯时间） |
| 预设 `datetime` | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`（带年份，不带方括号） |
| 预设回落 | 非法/缺省的 `preset` 一律归一化为默认的 `monthday` |
| **开关粒度** | **逐会话**。`sessions[sessionId]` 优先；该会话从没被用户动过开关时，回落到全局 `enabled`。⇒ 在一个对话里关掉**不会**影响其他对话 |
| 会话 id 来源 | Host 侧 `agent.session.id`（`Session.id` 取 `header.id`）；Client 侧取自槽位 standard props 的 `sessionId` |
| 开关落盘 | settings 路径写 `sessions` dict（Host 端 `Schema.dict(Schema.boolean())` + `.volatile()`）；兜底路径写 localStorage 的 `dsh-send-timestamp:sessions` JSON 表 |
| 预设粒度 | **全局**（格式偏好，不逐会话） |
| 注入形态 | **不改写用户原文**：时间戳作为一条独立合成消息追加在批次末尾 |
| 是否显示 | **不在对话框显示**。合成消息的 `source.kind !== 'user'`，Chat 侧经 `contextMessage()` 归为 `context` 节点；而 `isVisibleChatNode()` 会隐藏不含 `tool-addition`/`tool-removal` 块的 context 节点。用户气泡里只有原话，模型与持久会话记录里照样有时间 |
| 去重 | 末尾已是**当前预设同格式**的时间戳时不追加 |
| 斜杠命令 | `/` 开头（含前导空白）不追加 |
| 取时间时机 | `agent/pre-step` 回调里 `new Date()`，绝不在模块加载时取 |
| 触发条件 | 仅当这一批消息里存在 `role === 'user' && source.kind === 'user'` 的那条时才注入（纯插件上下文步骤不注入） |
| 消息身份 | 合成消息 `id` 用 `crypto.randomUUID()`，发布前 `deepFreeze`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand` 的 `brandString` 是编译期空操作，故与官方 `createUserMessage` 等价） |
| 空文本 | 无 text 片段的纯附件消息不追加 |

## 结构

```
package.json      bundle 声明：dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
cordis.patch.yml  - insert: 一行插件行；id `send-timestamp` 同时是设置命名空间
src/timestamp.ts  纯函数：格式化 / 追加 / 去重 / 斜杠判定（host 与 client 共用）
src/index.ts      host：Config（volatile）+ agent/pre-step 监听
src/client/index.tsx    client：槽位注册 + 按钮组件
src/client/toggle.ts    开关持久化的唯一接缝
src/client/styles.ts    主题 token 样式
scripts/build.mjs esbuild 构建
test/             node --test 单元测试与冒烟测试
lib/              构建产物（index.js / client.js / timestamp.js）
```

## 构建与测试

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # → lib/index.js、lib/timestamp.js、lib/client.js
npm test           # → node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

构建产物形态：

- `lib/index.js`：ESM，`platform: node`，`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 保持 external（profile 内已存在）。
- `lib/client.js`：esbuild 的 CJS 产物（`external: ['react']`，classic JSX）包进官方 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: '<npm 包名>', factory })` 外壳。
- `lib/timestamp.js`：纯函数层的独立 ESM 产物，供测试直接 import。

## 持久化

开关与预设走 **dsh 插件设置（profile 配置）**：Host 端 `Config` 用 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 声明，两个字段都 `.volatile()`——设置子系统只把 volatile 字段投影成条目表单，没有 volatile 字段的条目会被 `describe()` 整体跳过。Client 端通过 `ctx.configForms.get('send-timestamp')` 读取与写入（`entryId` 就是 `cordis.patch.yml` 里那一行的 `id`）。

`src/client/toggle.ts` 是唯一接缝：优先 `configForms`，其次第三方 `settingsScope`（`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings` 的兼容面），都不可用时退回 `localStorage`（键 `dsh-send-timestamp:enabled` / `dsh-send-timestamp:preset`）。任何一步失败都只降级、不抛错——组件抛错会让整条槽位条目变空白。

手动改默认值可直接编辑 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`：

```yaml
- id: send-timestamp
  name: '@local/dsh-send-timestamp'
  config: { enabled: true, preset: 'datetime' }
```

## 为什么改写发生在 Host 端

客户端**没有**任何 pre-submit 拦截点：Enter、发送按钮、`inputActions.submit()` 三条入口全部汇入 `SessionInputShell.submit(mode, source)`，且 `inputActions` 只暴露
`captureInsertion` / `insertText` / `setDraft` / `addAttachments` / `removeAttachment` / `pruneAttachments` / `submit` 七个方法，没有 `send` / `steer`。

唯一官方改写点是 `agent/pre-step` waterfall 的 `decision.messages`——它就是即将落库并送交模型的消息数组。改写时必须：

1. 先 `await next()`，并且不拥有决策；
2. `reject` / `signal.aborted` 原样放行；
3. **spread 决策对象**（`{ ...decision, messages }`），否则 `startsRequestSeries` 等字段会丢；
4. 消息对象是深冻结的且新铸了 id，所以只做浅拷贝并替换 `content`：`{ ...structuredClone(m), content }`，保留 `id` / `role` / `source`。

本插件不 import 任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 包（`schemastery` 除外），也不 import `dsh-llm`——那些包不在 profile 的 `node_modules` 里。

## 已知边界

- 时间戳追加在 `decision.messages` 上，而该数组正是随后 `session.append("user/message", ...)` 落库并送交模型的内容，因此落库的与模型看到的都是带时间戳的版本；输入框在**提交后立即清空**，所以界面上不会出现「你输入原文 vs 会话里带时间戳」的分叉。
- 未在真实浏览器里验证的部分：按钮的实际渲染位置与外观、`configForms` 写入是否真能落到 Host 的 profile 文档（依赖运行时服务在场）。
- 设置卡片刻意未实现：官方 `settings.plugin.item` 槽位在 0.2 已删除，现役落点是 `plugins.bundle.config`（key = 包名）或 `settings.plugins.tab`。开关本身就在输入框工具栏里，不需要卡片。

--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.

Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：/context 斜杠命令 + 上下文用量面板（占用构成、计费用量、轮数/步数/输出速度、账户余额）。零依赖、无构建。 | Zero-dependency DeepSeek Harness plugin: /context command and an at-a-glance context usage panel.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-context-usage

一个 **DeepSeek Harness** 的 Web 插件：把「这条对话到底把上下文烧到哪了」做成一屏可读的可视化面板 —— `/context` 斜杠命令、作曲器里的占用按钮、以及 composer 上方的用量总览。

> 对标 Claude Code 的 `/context`：同样的**分段占用 + 容量占比**，但补齐了它在 DSH 里缺失的部分 —— 累计计费用量、轮数/步数/输出速度、账户余额。

![面板截图](docs/screenshot.png)

---

## 它解决什么

DSH 原生的上下文信息散落在作曲器下方那条底栏里：一个圆环 + 三个计费药丸。你知道"用了多少"，但不知道 **用在哪**（系统提示词？工具定义？对话历史？），也看不到本会话的累计消耗和速度。

这个插件把那些数字集中成一块面板，并把官方底栏整行隐藏、把纵向空间还给对话区（隐藏项全部有去处，见下）。

## 功能

- **`/context` 斜杠命令** —— 带插件自有的图标与中文简介，一键开合面板
- **占用按钮** —— 作曲器控件行（发送键与模型选择器之间）的 `◔ 67%`，实时跟随，点击开合
- **用量面板** —— 作曲器上方，四块信息并排：
  - **总览**：三段圆环 + `666.1K / 1M` + 占比 + `轮数 · 步数 · tok/s`
  - **占用图**：36×5 的方块阵列，按 系统 / 工具 / 消息 三类着色，其余为自由空间
  - **本会话累计**：未命中 / 命中 / 命中率 / 输出（provider 计费口径）
  - **图例**：系统提示词 / 工具定义 / 对话消息 / 自由空间 的色块与数值
- **余额药丸** —— 作曲器右侧显示账户余额，前台每 10 秒刷新，悬停显示取样时间；未登录/无钱包/接口异常都有明确状态
- **零依赖、无构建** —— 手写纯 JavaScript，只 `require('react')`，样式只用宿主主题 token。没有 `src/`、没有 `pnpm install`、没有 `pnpm run build`

## 安装

> 安装**只能**通过 DSH 的 `plugin_manager` 工具完成 —— 这是官方唯一支持的路径（官方技能明确禁止手改 profile 的 `package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml`，也禁止在 profile 里自己跑 pnpm）。

**开发模式**（文件夹链接，改代码即时生效）：

```jsonc
plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "<本仓库的绝对路径>" }
```

**发布模式**（tarball 独立副本，本体可删可移）：

```powershell
powershell -File scripts\pack.ps1        # 生成 local-dsh-context-usage-<version>.tgz
```

```jsonc
plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "<tgz 的绝对路径>" }
```

装好后敲 `/context`，或点作曲器右下角（模型选择器与发送键之间）的 `◔ xx%` 按钮。

完整的验证 / 升级 / 卸载 / 迁移步骤见 **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**（那份是写给 agent 读的）。

## 它隐藏了官方底栏，那些信息去哪了

挂载时本插件会整行隐藏作曲器下方那条官方底栏（原版占用圆环 + 轮/步/速度药丸 + 计费用量药丸），信息全部有去处：

| 官方底栏 | 去向 |
|---|---|
| 占用率圆环 | 面板总览 + 作曲器占用按钮 |
| 未命中 / 命中 / 输出 / 计费 | 面板「本会话累计」 |
| 轮数 / 步数 / 输出速度 | 面板总览第三行 |
| 账户余额 | 作曲器控件行（占用按钮右侧） |

官方没有可用的开关 —— `ui-conversation` 的 Config 只有 `busyEnter` 一项；`conversation.input.activity` 槽虽然能抑制圆环，但同一处 `hidden: activity` 会把模型选择器和本插件按钮一起藏掉。

所以实现方式是**本插件自有的一张样式表**，作用域由本插件放进该 dock 的锚点元素限定：

```css
[class$="_dock"]:has([data-context-usage="composer-dock-anchor"]) { display: none !important }
```

- 只可能命中本插件锚点所在的那个 dock，不会波及其他面板
- 想恢复官方底栏：把 `client.js` 里的 `HIDE_SHIPPED_DOCK` 改成 `false`
- 依赖 `_dock` 这个 CSS Module 命名后缀，**DSH 大版本升级后需要复核一次**

## 数据来源与口径

数据全部来自宿主已有的投影，没有自算、没有埋点、不发额外请求：

| 面板元素 | 来源 | 口径 |
|---|---|---|
| 容量 / 占用 | `contextPressure.contextWindow`、`pressureTokens` | provider 每次请求上报，**换模型自动跟随**，包内不硬编码容量 |
| 系统 / 工具 / 消息 | `contextBreakdown` | 见下方说明 |
| 未命中 / 命中 / 命中率 / 输出 | `tokenUsage` | provider 上报的**计费**口径（本会话累计） |
| 轮数 / 步数 / 输出速度 | `sessionStats` | 宿主统计 |
| 余额 | `ctx.remote.account.getBalance` | 宿主直连 Platform，**宿主侧无缓存** |

两点如实说明：

1. **占用图的三段构成是估算**：`contextBreakdown` 给出三段 token 数，但方块按"每 token 约 4 字符"折算格数，与真实 token 边界不严格等价。占用率本身（`pressureTokens / contextWindow`）是精确上报值。
2. **"本会话累计"与"占用图"不同源**：前者是计费口径的累计值，后者是当前请求的上下文构成。两者不该互相验算，这是有意保留的。

## 已知边界

- 只在 **Web / 桌面 GUI** 里有命令面（纯客户端命令），headless / CLI 没有该命令
- 上下文容量取自 provider 上报值，模型没上报时该行按缺失处理
- 余额药丸里的 `CLIENT_VERSION` 硬编码为 `0.2.0-rc.2`（客户端插件运行时读不到 shell 版本）。DSH 升级后若平台拒收，药丸会显示 `余额 接口异常·<code>`，改这一处常量即可
- 包名 `@local/dsh-context-usage` 里的 `@local` 是"只装进本机 profile、从不发布到 npm"的意思，不是真实的 npm scope；`private: true` 同理

## 目录结构

```
package.json        # 包清单：dsh.bundle.patch（Host 行）+ dsh.client（浏览器半）+ icon + locale
cordis.patch.yml    # 一行 insert，把本包挂进 profile 条目树
index.js            # Host 半：空壳（不注册任何东西）
client.js           # Client 半：全部逻辑（约 800 行手写 JS）
locale/zh.json      # 插件页展示的标题与描述
locale/en.json
icon.svg            # 插件页图标（三段圆环）
scripts/pack.ps1    # 打包成可独立安装的 tarball
INSTALL.md          # 写给 agent 的安装/卸载/迁移说明
docs/               # README 配图
```

## 开发

改 `client.js` → 开发模式下页面自动热更；如果页面仍跑着旧 bundle（浏览器会按 id 去重注册），在插件管理里 disable → enable 再 `Ctrl+R`。Host 半（`index.js`）改动需要重启 DSH。

## 卸载

```jsonc
plugin_manager { "action": "remove_bundle", "target": "@local/dsh-context-usage" }
```

然后检查 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`，删掉 plugin_manager 追加的覆盖项：

```yaml
- id: context-usage
  disabled: false
```

开发模式下**先卸载再删文件夹**。详见 [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)。

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DSH 原生「同花顺 AI」插件：复用本机已登录浏览器 profile 查询同花顺问财，提供右侧面板、/ths skill 与 ths_query/ths_status 工具。非官方。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ths-ai · 同花顺问财 DSH 插件

[![CI](https://github.com/buyou-claw/dsh-ths-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/buyou-claw/dsh-ths-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

把**同花顺问财（iwencai）**接进 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）：右侧多一个「同花顺 AI」面板，对话里多一个 `/ths` 命令，模型手里多两个工具 `ths_query` / `ths_status`。

> **它不是 API，也不是 MCP。** 它复用你**本机已经登录的浏览器 profile**，像你本人一样打开问财页面读取结果。
> 因此没有 API Key、没有服务端、没有任何数据离开你的电脑 —— 代价是你的账号、你的登录态、你所在平台的使用协议，责任都在你这边。**使用前请先读 [合规与免责声明](docs/LEGAL.md)。**

![面板截图](docs/assets/panel.png)

---

## 目录

- [它能做什么](#它能做什么)
- [环境要求](#环境要求)
- [安装](#安装)
- [首次使用](#首次使用)
- [两种使用方式](#两种使用方式)
- [配置项](#配置项)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)
- [隐私与安全](#隐私与安全)
- [项目结构](#项目结构)
- [开发与测试](#开发与测试)
- [Roadmap](#roadmap)
- [许可](#许可)

---

## 它能做什么

| 能力 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 右侧面板 | 输入自然语言问题 → 直接拿回问财表格；显示登录状态、可一键登录、可刷新状态 |
| `/ths <问题>` | 对话里让 AI 调用工具查问财，并把结果总结成「结论 + 精简表格 + 口径 + 异常项」，而不是甩一张原始表格 |
| `ths_query` 工具 | 模型可直接调用：`{"query": "最近一周涨幅最大的个股"}` |
| `ths_status` 工具 | 只读判断当前 profile 是否已登录（不猜、不编） |
| 状态缓存 | 状态检查要拉起一次浏览器（10–20 s），因此结果缓存 5 分钟并启动后台预热，面板打开基本秒回 |
| 查询节流 | 两次查询之间默认强制 ≥3 秒间隔，避免把问财打到限流 |

**它不是什么：**

- 不是行情数据源：没有内置数据、没有行情缓存，不保证数据完整或实时；
- 不是投资建议工具：结果来自问财页面，内容由 AI 生成，请自行甄别；
- 不绕过登录 / 验证码 / 付费墙，也不内置任何反检测隐身参数；
- 不承诺跨平台：**Windows + Edge 是实测路径**，其它平台见 [配置项](#配置项)。

## 环境要求

| 依赖 | 要求 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness | `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` | 0.2.x 起 agent 工具必须声明 `output { schema, render }` |
| Node.js | `>= 20` | 用 DSH 自带运行时即可，无需单独安装 |
| 浏览器 | Edge（默认） | 走 Playwright `channel: 'msedge'`，用**系统已安装**的 Edge，不下载内核 |
| 账号 | 你自己的同花顺问财账号 | 登录在可见窗口里由你本人完成 |
| 平台 | Windows（实测） | macOS / Linux 见 `DSH_THS_BROWSER` |

> 只依赖 `playwright-core`（约 13 MB，不含浏览器二进制），`npm install` 不会触发浏览器下载。

## 安装

### 方式 A：一键脚本（Windows，推荐）

```powershell
# 1. 把仓库放到 DSH 插件目录
git clone https://github.com/buyou-claw/dsh-ths-ai "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\plugins\dsh-ths-ai"

# 2. 装依赖并接进 DSH 桌面端 profile
cd "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\plugins\dsh-ths-ai"
npm install --omit=dev
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install\install.ps1

# 3. 重启 DSH 桌面端
```

脚本做三件事：① 在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 登记依赖与 bundle（先备份为 `package.json.bak-ths-ai`）；② 建 `node_modules/dsh-ths-ai` 目录联接；③ 打印下一步。可重复运行（幂等）。

### 方式 B：手工（任何平台）

1. 把仓库放到 `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-ths-ai`，执行 `npm install --omit=dev`；
2. 编辑 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`：
   ```json
   {
     "dependencies": { "dsh-ths-ai": "file:../../plugins/dsh-ths-ai" },
     "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "...原有项", "dsh-ths-ai" ] } }
   }
   ```
3. 建联接：Windows `New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-ths-ai" -Target "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\plugins\dsh-ths-ai"`；macOS/Linux 用 `ln -s`；
4. 重启 DSH。

完整步骤（含校验与卸载回滚）见 [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md)。

### 验证安装

1. 右侧栏应出现「同花顺 AI」面板；
2. 对话里发 `/ths 今日涨幅前10的股票`，应直接返回结果；
3. 工具注册情况见 `~/.dsh/logs/dsh-ths-ai.log`：应有 `ths_query registered` / `ths_status registered`。

> 工具没出现？先看下面「常见问题」，90% 是 DSH 版本或没重启。

## 首次使用

1. 打开右侧「同花顺 AI」面板 → 点 **登录问财**；
2. 弹出的浏览器窗口里用**你自己的账号**完成登录；
3. **登录完成后关闭那个窗口**（登录态已写入本地 profile）；
4. 回面板点 **刷新状态**，出现「已登录」即可查询。

> 同一个 profile 同时只能被一个浏览器进程使用。登录窗口开着时不要查询，会报 profile 被占用。

## 两种使用方式

**面板**：随手查，结果直接渲染成表格。

**对话 `/ths`**：

```text
/ths 最新一周涨幅最大的个股
/ths 低市盈率且主力净流入的股票
/ths status          # 只看登录状态
```

AI 会调用 `ths_query` 取数，再按「结论 → 精简表格 → 口径 → 异常项（ST/新股/北交所/单日大跌但区间大涨）」组织回答，不编数据。

## 配置项

全部通过环境变量覆盖，**不设置时行为与默认完全一致**：

| 变量 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_THS_PROFILE_DIR` | `<插件目录>/profile` | 浏览器持久化配置目录。装到只读目录时改成可写路径 |
| `DSH_THS_BROWSER` | `msedge` | Playwright channel。macOS/Linux 可试 `chrome` / `chromium`（未实测，欢迎反馈） |
| `DSH_THS_WAIT_MS` | `12000` | 结果页渲染等待毫秒数。网络慢/表格空可上调 |
| `DSH_THS_STATUS_WAIT_MS` | `3500` | 状态检查页等待毫秒数 |
| `DSH_THS_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | `3000` | 两次查询的最小间隔（节流） |
| `DSH_THS_LOG_DIR` | `~/.dsh/logs` | 诊断日志目录（`dsh-ths-ai.log`，超过 512 KB 自动清空） |
| `DSH_THS_NODE` | 自动探测 | 指定用哪个 node 跑子进程（默认用 DSH 自带运行时） |

## 常见问题

| 现象 | 最可能的原因 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| 面板能用，但模型说没有 `ths_query` 工具 | DSH 版本不匹配 / 未重启 | 确认 DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2`；重启桌面端；看 `~/.dsh/logs/dsh-ths-ai.log` |
| 登录状态一直「检查中…」很久 | 首次检查要拉起浏览器（10–20 s），之后走缓存 | 等一次即可；之后 5 分钟内秒回 |
| 提示「未登录」但明明登录过 | 查询与登录用的不是同一个 profile | 统一 `DSH_THS_PROFILE_DIR`；登录后关闭窗口再刷新状态 |
| `browser has been closed` / profile 被占用 | 登录窗口还开着，或并发查询 | 关掉登录窗口；不要并发 |
| 返回 `blocked` / 访问受限 | 触发问财限流或风控 | 调大 `DSH_THS_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`，过段时间再试 |
| 表格列为空 / 结构错乱 | 问财前端改版 | 带日志开 issue |
| macOS/Linux 报 browser not found | 默认 channel 是 `msedge` | `DSH_THS_BROWSER=chrome` 或 `chromium` |

完整排查树见 [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)。

**提 issue 请附**：DSH 版本、操作系统、`~/.dsh/logs/dsh-ths-ai.log` 相关片段、复现用问句。**不要贴 Cookie / 账号信息。**

## 隐私与安全

- 登录态（Cookie，含 `u_ukey`）只存在**本机** `profile/` 目录，插件不上传任何数据；`.gitignore` 已排除 `profile/`。
- 想彻底清除登录态：关掉 DSH → 删除 `profile/` 目录（下次重新登录）。
- 不要在 issue / 截图里暴露 Cookie、手机号、验证码。
- 安全问题的报告流程见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

## 项目结构

```text
dsh-ths-ai/
├── index.js            # 宿主侧：路由 /ths-ai/*、2 个 agent 工具、子进程桥、状态缓存
├── client.js           # 客户端侧：右侧「同花顺 AI」面板
├── config.mjs          # 运行期配置（目录 / 浏览器 channel / 等待时间 / 日志）
├── login.mjs           # 打开可见窗口让你本人登录
├── query.mjs           # 无头打开问财、抽取表格、输出 THS_RESULT
├── status.mjs          # 只读判断登录态、输出 THS_STATUS
├── cordis.patch.yml    # DSH bundle patch：注册插件
├── skills/ths/SKILL.md # /ths skill 指令（模型侧行为约束）
├── docs/               # 安装 / 排查 / 架构 / 合规
└── install/            # 一键安装与卸载脚本
```

细节见 [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)。

## 开发与测试

```bash
npm install --omit=dev
npm run check            # 6 个文件语法检查（CI 跑这个）
npm run verify:status    # 真实检查登录态（会拉起浏览器）
THS_QUERY="今日涨幅前10的股票" npm run verify:query   # 真实查询一次
```

CI 只做语法检查，不做联网测试（不在 CI 里使用任何账号）。改动问财选择器时请本地跑 `verify:query` 并附日志。

贡献流程见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)，Issue/PR 约定见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)，版本发布与市场提交见 [docs/PUBLISHING.md](docs/PUBLISHING.md)。

## Roadmap

- [ ] macOS / Linux 浏览器探测实测（当前靠 `DSH_THS_BROWSER` 手动指定）
- [ ] 用 `waitForSelector` 替换固定 12 s 等待，缩短查询耗时
- [ ] 表格结构适配层：问财改版时集中改一处
- [ ] 结构化输出（`ths_query` 返回 JSON，便于二次加工）
- [x] 上架 DSH 插件市场（GitHub topic `dsh-plugin`，见 [docs/PUBLISHING.md](docs/PUBLISHING.md)）

> **Release compatibility:** The current tested Host is official `0.2.0-rc.2`. SeekTTY `1.3.0` is paired with that Host. See the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md) for changes and installation, and the [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md) for exact package evidence.

SeekTTY

A terminal workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

Overview · Quick start · Clarify and Plan · Features · Compatibility

English · 中文

--- ## Overview Run `deepseek` from a project directory to use the native Agent, Session, model, permission, Settings, Profile, plugin, and persistence services of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in one terminal workspace. SeekTTY is the terminal surface; Harness remains the owner of runtime state. Models, Providers, Agent Presets, permissions, commands, tools, Settings, Skills, MCP servers, and marketplace sources are discovered from the running Harness. Capabilities added by upstream or third-party Bundles therefore appear without being hard-coded into SeekTTY. For requirements that still need definition, the optional [Clarify Host plugin](https://github.com/Hilbert-beinghappy/dsh-plugin-clarify) adds a guided `/clarify` workflow. It asks focused questions, updates a reviewable Draft after each answer, and returns the accepted Draft to the composer. Harness-native `/plan` can then turn the submitted requirement into an implementation plan. ## Development checkout Build and install a local SeekTTY package from the repository root: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm run build pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false ./seektty-1.3.0.tgz dsh --profile tui ``` Use the local tarball for source development and testing. For the released package, use the exact npm version below. ## Quick start Install the published SeekTTY release on its verified official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 dsh --profile tui ``` These commands install the prebuilt Bundle through native `dsh plugin` reconciliation. The per-command pnpm option avoids the pnpm 11 Global Virtual Store layout that the Cordis loader in the currently tested dsh releases cannot reliably load. SeekTTY never changes global pnpm configuration. Clarify and Auxiliary Runtime are optional, not default dependencies; their historical joint acceptance is listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-verification). The exact `seektty@1.3.0` npm package is documented in the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### Bare `deepseek` launcher After installing `dsh`, install the same SeekTTY release globally and pin Profile reconciliation to its exact npm version: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 export SEEKTTY_SPEC=seektty@1.3.0 deepseek ``` PowerShell uses the same exact npm spec: ```powershell pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false 'seektty@1.3.0' $env:SEEKTTY_SPEC='seektty@1.3.0' deepseek ``` `deepseek` requires `dsh` on `PATH`, or `DSH_BIN` pointing to its executable. Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that intercepts repeated tool calls, caps per-turn budgets, and breaks failure loops to reduce token waste.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tool-governor

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that stops runaway tool calls before they burn through your token budget.

## What it does

- **Repeat-call breaker** — denies the same tool + argument combination after N repeats
- **Per-turn budget fuse** — hard-caps tool calls and model steps per turn
- **Failure-loop cutoff** — pauses a tool after consecutive failures
- **Monotonic guard** — denies are final; downstream layers cannot re-allow a blocked call

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tool-governor
```

Restart DSH after installing. Verify the bundle is registered:

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | findstr dsh-tool-governor
```

Pin a version, or install directly from source:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tool-governor@1.0.1
dsh plugin --profile web add github:George-Java/dsh-tool-governor
```

## Compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `0.2.x` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.2`) |
| Platform | Windows / macOS / Linux |
| Node.js | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |

The plugin hooks `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `ctx.tools.guard`, and `agent/pre-step`
at the profile root, so it needs only the global `tools` service. It reads the acting agent from
`exec.agent` / `event.agent`, and takes the current turn from the `agent/pre-step` payload
(`event.turn`), falling back to `agent.currentTurn` on 0.1.x. A new turn starts a fresh budget.

## Configuration

All fields are optional — defaults are applied when omitted.

| Field | Default | Description |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `maxToolCallsPerTurn` | `24` | Max tool calls allowed in one turn |
| `maxStepsPerTurn` | `16` | Max model steps allowed in one turn |
| `repeatThreshold` | `2` | Deny after the same call repeats this many times |
| `consecutiveFailureThreshold` | `2` | Pause a tool after N consecutive failures |
| `denyTools` | `[]` | Glob patterns of tools to always deny (e.g. `["browser_*"]`) |
| `denyMessage` | built-in | Message injected when a call is denied |

Override through the profile `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-tool-governor
  name: dsh-tool-governor
  config:
    maxToolCallsPerTurn: 12
    repeatThreshold: 1
```

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tool-governor
```

## How it works

1. `tools/pre-execute` — denies blacklisted tools, exhausted per-turn budgets, repeated signatures, and failure loops.
2. `tools/post-execute` — counts completed calls and tracks consecutive failures.
3. `ctx.tools.guard` — a monotonic, synchronous guard that makes earlier denials final.
4. `agent/pre-step` — records the current turn for every agent and rejects the turn once its model-step budget is spent.

Per-agent, per-turn ledgers are keyed by agent id and turn number.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Codex-style selection quote annotations for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-codex-annotate · 划词引用回复

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的 Web UI 加一个 Codex 风格的「划词追问」：选中助手回复里的任意文字，右键选择 **在此回答**，写下你的问题或补充；可以连续攒下多条注释，最后一次性发出。发出的消息自带精确出处（消息 id、轮次、段号、小节、字符区间或代码行号）和原文，并在气泡里折叠成一条 `📎 N 条注释` 的附件条。

> 面向 DSH **0.2.1-rc.2** 的 Web 客户端构建，依赖若干尚未承诺稳定的 DOM / React 内部细节（见[兼容性](#兼容性与已知限制)）。

## 特性

- **划词右键即用**：右键菜单里新增「在此回答」，与「复制」并列；没有选中文字时不拦截系统菜单。
- **精确定位**：消息 id、轮次、段号、所在小节标题、字符区间；代码块记录语言与行号。
- **先确认、后统一发送**：每次确认只暂存一条注释，输入框工具行显示 `📎 N 条注释`，点开可逐条删除或清空，最后一次性发送。
- **气泡内折叠**：发出的消息把引用部分收成 `📎 N 条注释 ▾`，点击展开原文，展开后仍可正常划选复制。
- **纯本地**：没有任何网络请求或遥测；引用内容就是一条普通用户消息，fork / 回放 / 搜索 / 上下文压缩都照常工作。

## 环境

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2**（Web UI 或桌面版）
- 无构建步骤：仓库里的 `client.js` 就是浏览器直接加载的模块

## 安装

要求 DSH 已安装且 `dsh` 在 PATH 中。从 GitHub 直接安装：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:mar1259/dsh-plugin-codex-annotate
```

`desktop` 是桌面版的 profile 名；Web 版通常用 `web`，换成你实际启动的 profile 即可。
固定到某个 commit，避免仓库后续改动影响现有环境：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:mar1259/dsh-plugin-codex-annotate#<commit-sha>
```

本地 clone 安装：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mar1259/dsh-plugin-codex-annotate.git
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-plugin-codex-annotate
```

卸载：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-codex-annotate
```

本仓库是纯 JS，没有 `prepare` / `build` 脚本，git 安装不需要 pnpm 的 `allowBuilds` 许可。

> 安装或更新客户端 bundle 后，刷新页面（或重启 DSH）才会加载新的 JS 代际。

## 使用

1. 在助手回复中选中一段文字 → **右键** → `❝ 在此回答`。
2. 在弹出的输入框里写下回复 → 点 **确认**（或按 Enter）。
3. 继续划词、继续确认；输入框工具行左侧出现 `📎 N 条注释` 胶囊。
4. 点胶囊 → 浮层里可逐条删除、清空，或直接 **发送**。
5. 发送后，所有注释与回复合成**一条**用户消息；气泡里显示为 `📎 N 条注释 ▾`，点击展开。

## 发出的消息长这样

段落选区：

```text
> **回复引用** · 助手消息 #4f2a1c · 第 3 轮 · 第 2 段「方案 A」· 字符 12–58
> 「建议把鉴权放到网关层，避免每个服务重复实现。」

那网关自己挂了怎么办？
```

代码选区：

```text
> **回复引用** · 助手消息 #4f2a1c · 第 3 轮 · 代码块 ts · 第 12–18 行
> ```
> for (const x of xs) { ... }
> ```
```

多条注释会按顺序拼接在同一个消息里，每条一个引用块 + 一段回复。

## 工作原理

| 部件 | 挂载点 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 右键菜单 + 引用编辑器 + 注释列表 | `shell.overlay` | 全帧浮层：拦截助手选区上的 `contextmenu`，渲染菜单/编辑器/列表 |
| 待发送胶囊 | `conversation.input.left` | 输入框工具行左侧，显示 `📎 N 条注释` |
| 发送桥 | `conversation.input.overlay` | 从会话作用域拿到 `inputActions`，把文本写入输入框并提交 |
| 气泡折叠 | 注入 CSS + DOM 标记 | 给用户气泡内的引用 `<blockquote>` 打标记，折叠成附件条 |

- 消息身份不依赖 CSS 类名：从选区节点沿 React fiber 链读取 `sessionId` / `messageId` / 轮次，读不到时退回 `data-chat-flow-kind` 属性。
- 发送走宿主自己的输入管线：`insertText`（追加到草稿末尾）或 `setDraft`，随后 `submit()`，因此排队、steer、附件等行为与手动发送一致。
- 引用内容始终是消息正文的一部分，没有被藏进自定义事件；`<blockquote>` 折叠只是视觉呈现。

## 兼容性与已知限制

- 依赖 DSH 客户端内部结构：`__reactFiber$*`、`data-chat-flow-kind` / `data-chat-turn`、用户消息里 `<blockquote>` 的渲染方式。**升级 DSH 后可能需要适配**。
- 目前只支持助手回复正文；跨消息选择、工具调用卡片、流式输出中的消息不会出现菜单项。
- 待发送注释只存在内存里，刷新页面会清空。
- 在助手选区的右键菜单会**替换**系统菜单，当前只提供「复制」与「在此回答」两项；其他区域仍使用系统菜单。
- 长引用会截断：正文 300 字、代码 12 行，超出会标注「已截断」。
- 若输入框在确认到发送之间被改动，发送会中止并提示重试，避免覆盖你的草稿。

## 隐私

插件不做任何网络请求，不收集遥测，也不读写工作区文件。引用的原文与你的回复会作为普通消息文本，经 DSH 原有的发送链路交给模型。

## 开发

仓库即包目录，没有构建产物：

```text
client.js          # 浏览器半边：菜单、编辑器、注释列表、气泡折叠
index.js           # Host 半边：空 apply，仅用于打包
cordis.patch.yml   # Bundle 补丁：插入一行 codex-annotate
package.json       # dsh.bundle / dsh.client 清单
locale/{zh,en}.json# 插件管理器显示的标题与描述
icon.svg           # 插件图标
```

语法自检：

```bash
node --check client.js
node --check index.js
```

## 贡献者

- [mar1259](https://github.com/mar1259) — 作者、产品方向与测试
- **DeepSeek Harness Agent** — AI 结对实现（架构、客户端代码、文档）

提交记录中使用 `Co-authored-by: DeepSeek Harness Agent <agent@dsh.invalid>` 标注 AI 协作；这是保留域名的占位邮箱，不对应任何公开账号。

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 mar1259

---

## English

Codex-style selection annotations for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI. Select text in an assistant reply, right-click, choose **Reply here**, write your note, and confirm — accumulate several notes as a `📎 N notes` chip inside the composer tool row, then send them all at once. The outgoing message quotes the exact location (message id, turn, block, section, character range or code lines) and is folded into an expandable attachment row inside the chat bubble.

Install:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:mar1259/dsh-plugin-codex-annotate
```

Tested against DSH 0.2.1-rc.2. The plugin relies on client internals (`__reactFiber$`, `data-chat-flow-kind`, rendered blockquotes), so DSH upgrades may require adaptation. No network access, no telemetry. MIT licensed.

Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: A panel for the servers and static pages an agent started on localhost: port, directory, registering session, and one switch to stop each.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-localhost > 一个面板，回答"这台机器上现在跑着什么、哪个目录、哪个会话开的、怎么关掉"。 agent 在开发里起服务是常态：`pnpm dev`、`python -m http.server`、一个 `dist/` 静态页。它们是短暂的，但**不会自己消失**——三个小时后你没死，那个端口也没死。这个插件把"起服务"变成一次**登记**，于是端口不用猜、目录不会丢、关掉有地方点。
中文 ## 它做什么 **两种东西，都归它管；第三种它老实承认管不了。** | 类型 | 谁在跑 | 生命周期 | |---|---|---| | `静态页` | 插件自己（127.0.0.1 上的一个小服务器） | 跟着 DSH 一起关 | | `命令` | 插件通过 Harness 的 subprocess 服务启动 | 插件停它就停，DSH 退出时全部停 | | 别的进程 | agent 自己用 bash 起的 | **不在这里**。杀不掉的进程不该显示成"运行中" | 这不是洁癖。一个后台进程如果没人拥有，它就会活过它该活的时间——见 [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md) 里那四个活了十一天的东西。 ## 装 ``` github:kjx-talesofai/dsh-plugin-localhost#v0.3.0 ``` 装完**重启桌面端**（host 半边只在启动时加载）。 ## agent 怎么用 给 agent 的是一个工具 `serve`，不是一堆 bash： ```jsonc { "action": "register", "kind": "spawned", "name": "preview", "dir": "/path/to/project", "cmd": "pnpm dev --port $PORT", "path": "/" } { "action": "register", "kind": "static", "name": "deck", "dir": "/path/to/dist" } ``` 返回里带 `port` 和 `url`。**端口是插件分的（8840–8899），不是 agent 挑的**——所以"这个工作区开过哪些服务"这个问题有答案，而不是靠回忆。 其他动作：`list` / `start` / `stop` / `logs`。`logs` 返回最近的输出，排错不用截图。 ## 面板 侧边栏里，紧挨在 Tailscale Remote Access 下面。每行：状态点、名字、类型、端口、状态。展开后有： - **目录** —— 点「用 Finder 打开」 - **入口文件**（静态页）—— 点「显示入口文件」，Finder 里直接选中它 - **登记会话** —— 点「跳到会话」，回到当初开它的那个对话 - **日志** —— 最近 400 行，运行中会自己滚 行上的按钮：打开 / 启动 / 停止 / 收起。 ## 老实说（边界） - **只登记它自己起的**。agent 用 bash 起的服务，这个面板看不见——它杀不掉，就不能声称拥有。 - **DSH 退出 = 全部停止**。重启后所有条目显示"已停止"，需要手动点启动；不会偷偷帮你拉起来。 - **端口是分给它的**，所以别在别的脚本里硬编码 8840。想要固定端口就在 `cmd` 里自己用 `$PORT`。 - **静态页由它自己发**，不是复制文件：`dir` 改了立刻生效，`dir` 删了就 404。 - **只在 127.0.0.1 上**。这个端口没有认证，不要以为它是个"分享"按钮；要给别人看，走 Tailscale。 - **从手机打开**：面板会读 `tailscale serve status`，把已经发布到 tailnet 的端口配上远端地址；此时「打开」在**你的手机浏览器**里打开那个地址，而不是让 Mac 弹浏览器。没发布的端口在手机上不给「打开」按钮，并明说只在本机可访问。 - 静态页的 SPA 回退**只对浏览器导航生效**（`Accept: text/html`），这样 `/etc/hosts` 这类路径不会假装成路由。 ## Compatibility 实测于 **macOS（Apple Silicon）+ DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.2**。依赖的上游契约： | 契约 | 来自 | |---|---| | `webServer.register({ kind: 'exact', path })`，以及 `connection.admit(req)` 的准入栅栏 | `dsh-host-webserver`、`dsh-api-remotes` | | `subprocess.spawn` 的句柄、`collected.*.readFrom(offset)`、`terminate()`，以及**服务销毁时杀掉所有在管进程** | `dsh-subprocess-local` | | `ctx.tools.register` 的 `ToolDefinition`（`parameters` 里 `required` 写在字段内） | `dsh-tools` | | `sidebar.panellist` / `main` 两个槽位，`order` 决定导航顺序 | `dsh-client-ui-sidebar`、`dsh-client-ui-layout` | | `locale.bind(ns)` 支持 `{name}` 插值 | `dsh-client-locale` | | `uiWorkspace.openSession(id)` 接受裸 session id | `dsh-client-ui-workspace` | ## 开发 ```sh npm test # 45 条，不需要安装任何依赖 ``` Host 半边没有运行时依赖，所以测试**真的 import 它**，用假 ctx 驱动：静态服务走真实 socket，spawned 走假 subprocess，断言的是 spawn 规格而不是"看起来跑了"。Client 半边按页面加载的方式在 `node:vm` 里求值，再用一个迷你 hooks 运行时把面板渲染出来断言。 没有构建步骤：`client.js` 就是发布物。
English ## What it does Two kinds of things, both owned; a third it refuses to pretend about: | Kind | Who runs it | Lifetime | |---|---|---| | `static` | this plugin (a small 127.0.0.1 server) | stops with DSH | | `command` | this plugin, through the Harness subprocess service | stops when asked, and on DSH exit | | anything else | the agent, with bash | **not listed here**. A process we cannot kill must not read as "running". | The agent gets one tool, `serve`, instead of a pile of bash: it registers a directory or a start command and comes back with the assigned port and URL. Ports come from 8840–8899 and are assigned by the plugin, never typed by the agent — which is what makes "what did I start here" a question with an answer. The panel sits under Tailscale Remote Access: status, name, kind, port, and one switch. Expand a row for the directory (reveal in Finder), the entry file, the registering session (jump back to it), and the log tail. ## Honest limits - It lists only what it started. A server an agent began with bash is invisible — and unkillable — so it is not shown. - DSH exit stops everything; after a restart every entry reads stopped and nothing restarts itself. - Static pages are served from their directory, not copied; the port is not authenticated and is loopback-only. - The SPA fallback applies to browser navigations only (`Accept: text/html`), so a missing file stays a 404. ## Development ```sh npm test # 45 tests, no install step ``` The Host half has no runtime dependencies, so the suite imports it and drives a fake context: the static server over a real socket, the spawned path through a fake `ctx.subprocess`. The Client half is evaluated as a script in `node:vm` and rendered through a small hooks runtime.
## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Jiaxin Kou

plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. plugins.description: DSH plugin — free OpenCode Zen models for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Free LLM API, no API key needed. 在 DSH 中使用 OpenCode Zen 免费模型，无需 API key
plugins.readme_text:
# opencode2dsh **Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).** No API key. No registration. No extra process. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/blob/master/LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- opencode2dsh registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same models OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model picker as a regular provider called `opencode2dsh`. Requests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode CLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays fresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and nothing to host. ## Highlights - **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat - **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`) - **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation - **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Responses-only `muse-spark-*` models expose only upstream-supported effort levels, and no selection keeps the provider default - **Image input where it is declared** — image attachments are accepted for every model whose [models.dev](https://models.dev) entry lists `image` in `modalities.input`, and refused for the ones that declare `text` only; models.dev being silent falls back to the live-verified vision family - **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free-by-metadata, falling back to offline cache and a verified static list - **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics - **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH ## Install **From the plugin market** (recommended, once this repo is listed there): in DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `opencode2dsh`, one-click install. **From npm**: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin ``` **From source** (build the tarball yourself): ```sh git clone https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh.git cd opencode2dsh/packages/plugin pnpm install && pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./opencode2dsh-dsh-plugin-.tgz ``` **Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from the **opencode2dsh** group. Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 0.1.7 or newer with a web profile (the IP 池 settings page rides the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract); Node.js ≥ 20 (already present if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`. ## Configuration Defaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: opencode2dsh name: '@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin' config: mode: adapter # adapter (default) | sidecar providerId: opencode2dsh refreshSeconds: 300 # catalog refresh cadence ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. | | `providerId` | `opencode2dsh` | Provider name shown in DSH. | | `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. | | `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. | | `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. | | `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. | | `firstEventMs` / `bodyIdleMs` / `responsesBodyIdleMs` | `30000` / `120000` / `300000` | Adapter only, plugin 0.3.7+: stream-liveness watchdogs, in ms (integers from `1` to `600000`). Time to the first stream event, mid-response body silence, and the body-idle floor for Responses models (`muse-spark-*`). Increase `firstEventMs` for slow cold starts. Unset keeps the defaults; restart DSH after editing. | ## How it works ``` DSH session │ harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …) ▼ ZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter) │ pi-ai openai-completions stream (chat models) │ pi-ai openai-responses stream (`muse-spark-*`, Responses-only on Zen) ▼ https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 ← Authorization: Bearer public with CLI-identical headers: user-agent: opencode/… x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity, X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project ``` - **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible), and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI. - **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev pricing metadata decides "free"; S3: a compile-time verified static list. A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages. - **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic refresh. - **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)) on `127.0.0.1:`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary. ## Health & troubleshooting The plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round: ``` ~/.opencode2dsh/adapter-status.json ``` ```json { "status": "ready", "total": 64, "exposed": 9, "lastError": "", "writtenAt": "2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z" } ``` | Symptom | Likely cause & fix | | --- | --- | | `403 FreeTierError` / "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" | The upstream restricts free-tier clients. The plugin preserves the explanation instead of reporting an invalid API key. Use the supported OpenCode client or an official API service. | | Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot "plugins.item" requires options.id`, or the IP 池 entry has no configuration page | Your DSH predates the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract. Upgrade DSH to 0.1.7 (latest recommended). On 0.1.6 and older the page never mounts (it is gated on `configForms.whileServed`) — model routing is unaffected. | | DSH 0.1.7/0.2 cannot start after plugin installation (`pending … settingsScope`) | Upgrade the plugin to 0.3.5. On DSH 0.2, configure IP pooling through the installed opencode2dsh row on the Plugins page. | | Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. | | `lastError: "fetch failed"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. | | Rate-limit errors in chat (`429 … Endpoint is unavailable`) | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP and free models are contended. Since the fix for [#51](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/issues/51) the plugin's provider retry policy rides out 429 bursts silently (8 retries, ~1s→20s backoff, ≈90s worst case per step) instead of sur
